chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Karram, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who cut off a woman's finger. He said: 'Her finger is cut off until it reaches one-third of the woman [i.e., the depth of the finger]. If it goes beyond the one-third, the man is doubled [in compensation/diyyah].'
ai.seo_question: What is the limit of cutting a woman's finger in qisas according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a precise proportional limit for *qisas* (retaliation) in finger amputation, capping the depth at one-third of the woman's finger to prevent excessive retribution. The doubling of compensation (*diyyah*) for exceeding this limit reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing strict equality with mercy, ensuring that the punishment remains commensurate with the injury without becoming punitive beyond the actual harm caused.
